 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Atlanta Braves are ready to spend big to fix their biggest problem. Reports indicate the team will sign former Red Sox starter Sonny Gray to a massive deal worth $75 million. This move pairs a veteran winner with Chris Sale to create a deadly one-two punch for the rotation. Gray just finished a three-year stint with the Boston Red Sox where he proved he can still dominate at age 36.
 Gray brings a track record of winning that the Braves need badly. He led all of Major League Baseball with 18 wins in 2026. His 2.72 ERA for the Red Sox shows he can keep runs off the board. The Braves have struggled to find a reliable second ace behind Sale for years. This signing solves that issue with a player who knows how to pitch deep into games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A History of Pitching Woes
 The rotation has been a weak spot for Atlanta for a long time. Injuries have derailed the staff in 2026, leaving the team without a clear number two option. MLB.com's Jason Foster noted the issues before the trade deadline. "There are well-documented reasons why the Braves were in the market for a frontline starter at the Trade Deadline," Foster wrote. The team added Tyler Mahle, but he was not the difference-maker fans wanted.
 Now the pressure is on to get the rotation right before the 2027 season starts. Foster pointed out the specific gaps that need filling. "As the team heads down the stretch, there's now even more scrutiny on a few things: the lack of a potent 1-2 punch for the postseason, their bullpen's durability and the rotation's overall dependability," Foster wrote. Gray fits the profile of the durable arm the Braves have lacked.
 The Case for Sonny Gray
 Gray is not just a name on a list; he is a proven winner. Among only six pitchers, he stands as one who has logged 160 or more innings in every one of the past four seasons. Sports Illustrated's Will Laws believes the Braves will go after him hard. "Not many pitchers of Gray's age can command a multi-year deal, but he might just do it after recording a 2.72 ERA for the Red Sox and leading MLB in wins (18)," Laws wrote.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement His ability to pitch in different environments makes him a safe bet for Atlanta. He has not logged a below-average FIP since 2016. The only question is if Father Time will catch up to him soon. "The question is when Father Time will catch up with him," Laws wrote. For a team needing stability, Gray's consistency is exactly what they need right now.
 Fixing the 2027 Rotation
 The front office knows Chris Sale is the ace, but he cannot do it alone. SI's Harrison Smajovitts laid out the current state of the pitching staff. "Chris Sale is the ace. You probably guarantee that Bryce Elder is in the mix, too, along with Grant Holmes. After that, we'll see what happens," Smajovitts wrote. The rest of the rotation has been a mess, but Gray changes that dynamic immediately.
 Gray turns 37 in a few days, yet he is still one of the best starters available. Nashville, Tennessee is where he likes to play, as it is nearer to his home. The drive from Atlanta to Music City is short, making him a perfect fit for the local fan base. This connection might help seal the deal. The Braves have been linked to him for years, and this offseason looks like the right time to make it happen.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This signing is not just about adding a name; it is about winning games. Gray led the league in wins while dealing with a tough lineup in New York. He can eat innings and keep the team in the hunt. The $75 million price tag is steep, but the cost of a bad rotation is higher.
